title: Sequential thermoelastic analysis
summary: One isotropic material record supplies heat capacity, conductivity, elasticity, reference temperature, and thermal expansion to an implicit heat step followed by a thermal-stress solve, with conservative nonlinear enthalpy stepping for tabulated thermal properties and accepted-time field histories for sequential transfer.

science.statement: Temperature is solved first when mechanical response does not materially feed back into heat transfer, then thermal eigenstrain enters equilibrium as an equivalent load.

equations.label: heat equation
equations.description: Backward Euler advances the first-order thermal state.

equations.label: state-dependent heat increment
equations.description: Tabulated conductivity or specific heat selects a conservative nonlinear residual and automatic consistent Jacobian.

equations.label: thermal strain
equations.description: The reference temperature and dimensional reduction are explicit material/Study inputs.

equations.label: sequential stress equilibrium
equations.description: The thermal contribution remains a named inspectable vector operator.

equations.label: normalized Arrhenius factor
equations.description: The local creep coefficient retains its fitted meaning at the declared reference temperature.

inputs.name: thermomechanical properties
inputs.type: E, nu, rho, alpha, k, c_p, T_ref
inputs.description: One immutable material record shared by thermal and mechanical models.

inputs.name: temperature field
inputs.description: Solved or prescribed temperature consumed by thermal expansion or sampled at the receiving creep step's physical time.

inputs.name: temperature-dependent properties
inputs.description: Piecewise-linear tables preserve bounds, interpolation, provenance, and an explicit extrapolation policy.

outputs.name: thermal ledger
outputs.description: Sensible enthalpy, applied rate, outward rate, and discrete closure residual.

outputs.name: F_thermal
outputs.description: Equivalent load from constrained thermal expansion.

assumptions: Sequential coupling: temperature affects mechanics but mechanical dissipation and deformation do not feed back into heat transfer.
Temperature-dependent E, nu, and alpha are known coefficients in a sequential mechanical solve; heat-to-mechanics feedback remains one way.
Temperature-dependent conductivity and specific heat use piecewise-linear tables with explicit bounded extrapolation and an enthalpy primitive.
conventions: Plane strain retains the constrained out-of-plane thermal strain.
Plane stress uses the reduced in-plane constitutive law.
applicability: Thermal gradients and thermal stress in laboratory and power-plant component models when one-way coupling is adequate.
Preparing temperature fields for global Arrhenius creep integration.
limitations: No monolithic fully coupled temperature-displacement solve.
Convection is supported; radiation and general thermal contact are not yet included in this card.
Portable nodal histories are compact root-gathered archives rather than an extreme-scale parallel field database.
The nonlinear thermal route currently uses fixed physical time increments; adaptive thermal cutback and monolithic temperature-displacement coupling remain.

usage.minimal_example: Use materials.temperature_property(..., extrapolation='constant') for k(T) or cp(T), then call heat_step = model.step(target=temperature, dt=..., steps=...); capture its accepted temperature history and pass it to the Arrhenius creep step.

validation_rules: Reject nonpositive conductivity, specific heat, density, or absolute reference temperature.
Require an explicit 2D solid assumption for thermoelastic stress.
Reject silent temperature-history extrapolation and invalid or unordered property tables.
Reject simultaneous automatic tabulated thermal properties and user-supplied C/K operators; verify failed nonlinear-step rollback and checkpoint/restart equivalence.
